CleaningUp2 file has all the variable names changed and a bunch of stuff
brought to the top of the script.

I think it's probably basically all good. (I think CleaningUp1 has stuff brought
to front and more road-signs indicated where it originally came from, but no
variable name changes I think).

CleaningUp3 changed to revision objects, and entire first section updated
(so all the imports), although should probably write out all those matrices
and organize them in lists, etc.

CleaningUp4 will start slashing out unused code.

```{r}
theme_md_classic <- function() {
    theme_classic(
        base_size = 6, 
        base_family = "ArialMT",
        base_line_size = 0.25,
        base_rect_size = 0.25
    ) %+replace% theme(
        plot.title  = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 8),
        axis.title  = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.text   = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.ticks  = element_line(color = "black"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
        strip.text  = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        complete = TRUE
    )
}

theme_md_bw <- function() {
    theme_bw(
        base_size = 6, 
        base_family = "ArialMT",
        base_line_size = 0.25,
        base_rect_size = 0.25
    ) %+replace% theme(
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 6),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "black"),
        complete = TRUE
    )
}
```

# Utilities

## CPM normalization

```{r}
# rows are features, columns are samples
cpm <- function(mat) {
    t(1e6 * t(mat) / colSums(mat))
}
```

## Z-scoring

```{r}
# z-score each row in matrix
scale_rows <- function(m) {
    t(scale(t(m)))
}
```

## TF-TF network

```{r}
# Build an induced TF-TF network around a focal gene.
# - We first discover TF sets up to k_up hops upstream and k_down hops downstream,
#   only traversing through targets that are TFs.
# - Then we return all TF-TF edges among the union of discovered TFs (induced subgraph).
#
# Arguments:
#   gene    : focal gene symbol (character length 1)
#   ereg_df : data.frame with columns TF, Gene, eRegulon_name
#   k_up    : hops upstream (>= 0)
#   k_down  : hops downstream (>= 0)
#
# Returns: list(edges, nodes, groups)
#   - edges: tibble {eRegulon_name, TF, Gene, dir, src_group, tgt_group}
#   - nodes: tibble {TF, group} where group element of {up_d, center, down_d}
#   - groups: named list of character vectors (the layer sets you can print/inspect)
tf_neighborhood <- function(gene, ereg_df, k_up = 1, k_down = 1) {
    stopifnot(is.character(gene), length(gene) == 1)
    stopifnot(all(c("TF", "Gene", "eRegulon_name") %in% colnames(ereg_df)))
    stopifnot(k_up >= 0, k_down >= 0)
    
    edf <- ereg_df %>% filter(!is.na(TF), !is.na(Gene), !is.na(eRegulon_name))
    tf_set <- unique(edf$TF)
    
    groups <- list()
    
    # center (degree 0) — only included as a node label (doesn't have to be a TF)
    groups$center <- gene
    
    # upstream discovery (negative degrees)
    if (k_up > 0) {
        current <- gene
        for (d in seq_len(k_up)) {
            ups <- edf %>%
                filter(Gene %in% current) %>%
                pull(TF) %>%
                unique() %>%
                sort()
            if (length(ups) == 0) 
                break
            groups[[paste0("up_", d)]] <- ups
            current <- ups
        }
    }
    
    # downstream TF discovery (positive degrees) (only if gene is a TF)
    if (k_down > 0 && gene %in% tf_set) {
        current <- gene
        for (d in seq_len(k_down)) {
            downs <- edf %>%
                filter(TF %in% current, Gene %in% tf_set) %>%
                pull(Gene) %>%
                unique() %>%
                sort()
            if (length(downs) == 0) 
                break
            groups[[paste0("down_", d)]] <- downs
            current <- downs
        }
    }
    
    # node set: union of all discovered TFs
    node_set <- unique(unlist(groups, use.names = FALSE))
    
    # induced TF->TF edges among node_set
    # (dir=direction of regulation, +/- for activator/repressor)
    edges <- edf %>%
        filter(TF %in% node_set, Gene %in% node_set) %>%
        mutate(dir = sub(".*_(.*)/.*", "\\1", eRegulon_name)) %>% 
        distinct(eRegulon_name, TF, Gene, dir)
    
    # annotate nodes with their nearest group label (center, up_*, down_*)
    node_df <- tibble(TF = node_set, group = NA_character_)
    
    # prioritize center, then closest upstream/downstream layer
    assign_group <- function(x) {
        if (x %in% groups$center) 
            return("center")
        # smallest |degree| wins
        best <- NULL; best_abs <- Inf
        for (nm in names(groups)) {
            if (nm == "center") 
                next
            if (x %in% groups[[nm]]) {
                if (startsWith(nm, "up_")) {
                    deg <- -as.integer(sub("up_", "", nm))
                } else if (startsWith(nm, "down_")) {
                    deg <- as.integer(sub("down_", "", nm))
                } else {
                    deg <- 0L
                }
                if (abs(deg) < best_abs) { 
                    best <- nm
                    best_abs <- abs(deg)
                }
            }
        }
        if (is.null(best)) NA_character_ else best
    }
    node_df$group <- vapply(node_df$TF, assign_group, character(1))
    
    # add group labels to edges for convenience
    grp_map <- setNames(node_df$group, node_df$TF)
    edges <- edges %>%
        mutate(
            src_group = unname(grp_map[TF]),
            tgt_group = unname(grp_map[Gene])
        )
    
    list(edges = edges, nodes = node_df, groups = groups)
}
```

### Group genes/peaks by eRegulons

```{r}
# Target genes by regulon
ereg_neur_dir_pp_genes <- ereg_neur_dir_pp %>%
    group_by(eRegulon_name) %>%
    summarise(genes = list(unique(Gene)), .groups = "drop")

# Peaks by Regulon (if column name differs, change 'region')
ereg_neur_dir_pp_peaks <- ereg_neur_dir_pp %>%
  group_by(eRegulon_name) %>%
  summarise(peaks = list(unique(Region)), .groups = "drop")

# And now join (eRegulon_name, genes, peaks)
ereg_neur_dir_pp_both <- inner_join(ereg_neur_dir_pp_genes, ereg_neur_dir_pp_peaks, by = "eRegulon_name")
stopifnot(length(unique(ereg_neur_dir_pp$eRegulon_name)) == nrow(ereg_neur_dir_pp_both))
# > nrow(ereg_neur_dir_pp_both)
# [1] 188
# > length(unique(ereg_neur_dir_pp$TF))
# [1] 188
```

not a ton of TFs.

```{r}
# and direct repressors 
ereg_neur_dir_mp_genes <- ereg_neur_dir_mp %>%

ereg_neur_dir_mp_peaks <- ereg_neur_dir_mp %>%
```

## Modify obs

### Get "rg_cl": set of regionally localized neuronal clusters

For many (but not all) analyses, we will only use clusters that are spatially
localized to an anatomical structure.

```{r}
rg_cl <- rownames(filter(
    obs,
    Subcortex_Class_v4 != "Nonneuron",
    Cluster_Dominant_Region != "Multi"
))
```


### Make NT_MSN to separate MSNs

Separate the MSNs from other GABA neurons.

```{r}
obs$NT_MSN <- obs$Cluster_NT
obs$NT_MSN[grep("MSN", obs$Subcortex_Group_v4)] <- "MSN"
```

```{r}
obs$RegionNT <- paste0(obs$Cluster_Dominant_Region, "_", obs$NT_MSN)
```

```{r}
        "GPe MEIS2-SOX6 GABA", # was "GP MEIS2-SOX6 GABA" in preprint
        "OT D1 ICj",
        "STRd D1 Matrix MSN",
        "STRd D1 Striosome MSN",
        "STR D1D2 Hybrid MSN", # was "STRd D1D2 Hybrid MSN" in preprint
        "STRd D2 Matrix MSN",
        "STRd D2 StrioMat Hybrid MSN",
        "STRd D2 Striosome MSN",
        "STRv D1 MSN",
        "STRv D2 MSN"
    )
)
stopifnot(all(unlist(ge_groups) %in% obs$Subcortex_Group_v4))
```

##### Mutate obs

Note I'm doing this after making `obs_sub` just to show these print-outs.

[!] GE, GE_RegionNT, etc. are effectively only going to be used for spatially
located clusters (in `rg_cl`), so there isn't even much point in putting these
new columns in the complete `obs`.

```{r}
nm_map <- setNames(
    rep(names(ge_groups), lengths(ge_groups)),
    unname(unlist(ge_groups))
)

obs$GE <- ifelse(
    obs$Subcortex_Group_v4 %in% names(nm_map),
    nm_map[obs$Subcortex_Group_v4],
    NA
)
```

##### Make GE_RegionNT

The column `GE_RegionNT` will be NA for everything not GE-derived. In hindsight
I could have dealt with this more elegantly, but it's slightly convenient in
many plots to just show the GE-derived cells and nothing else.

```{r}
obs <- mutate(
    obs,
    GE_RegionNT = ifelse(
        is.na(GE),
        NA,
        paste0(GE, "_", RegionNT)
    )
)


# > table(obs[rg_cl, "GE_RegionNT"])
```

##### Also make complete GE_RegionNT_Complete

Unlike `GE_RegionNT`, this won't be NA for non-GE-derived, but will instead
use `RegionNT` unless there's a value for `GE_RegionNT`.

So when this variable is used, all RegionNT will be shown (with GE-derived
cells divided out).

```{r}
obs$GE_RegionNT_Complete <- ifelse(
    is.na(obs$GE_RegionNT),
    as.character(obs$RegionNT),
    as.character(obs$GE_RegionNT)
)
```

## Z-score AUCell scores

For direct +/+ eRegulons, we expect both modalities to be high. Combine by 
z-scoring each matrix (per regulon across clusters) and averaging:

```{r}
geneAUC_neur_by_cl_z <- scale_rows(geneAUC_neur_by_cl)
peakAUC_neur_by_cl_z <- scale_rows(peakAUC_neur_by_cl)
```

```{r}
geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_cl_z <- scale_rows(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_cl)
peakAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_cl_z <- scale_rows(peakAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_cl)
```

### AUCell z-score means by Group, Class

For regulon AUC scores, will use the cluster-level z-scores, and average them.

```{r}
geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_group_z <- t(apply(
    geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_cl_z, 1, function(x) tapply(x, obs$Subcortex_Group_v4, mean)
))
geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_class_z <- t(apply(
    geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_cl_z, 1, function(x) tapply(x, obs$Subcortex_Class_v4, mean)
))
```

```{r}
peakAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_group_z <- t(apply(
    peakAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_cl_z, 1, function(x) tapply(x, obs$Subcortex_Group_v4, mean)
))
peakAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_class_z <- t(apply(
    peakAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_cl_z, 1, function(x) tapply(x, obs$Subcortex_Class_v4, mean)
))
```

```{r}
for (nt in colnames(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_nt_z)) {

    invisible(dev.off())
}
```

### Compare groups by shared regulons

#### RegionNT

Define “active regulons” per group (z>1), then compute Jaccard overlaps to see
which RegionNTs share the most regulons:

```{r}
act_by_regionnt <- lapply(colnames(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_rgnt_z), function(cn) {
    names(which(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_rgnt_z[,cn] > 1))
})
names(act_by_regionnt) <- colnames(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_rgnt_z)

# pairwise Jaccard
jaccard <- outer(
    names(act_by_regionnt), names(act_by_regionnt),
    Vectorize(function(a,b){
        A <- act_by_regionnt[[a]]
        B <- act_by_regionnt[[b]]
        length(intersect(A,B)) / length(union(A,B))
    })
)
rownames(jaccard) <- colnames(jaccard) <- names(act_by_regionnt)
```

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=10}
Heatmap(jaccard, name="Jaccard")
```

Fantastic

```{r}
pdf(
    file.path(pdir_ereg, "heatmap_jaccard_ereg_rgnt_thresh_z1.pdf"), 
    width = 8, height = 6
)
Heatmap(jaccard, name="Jaccard")
invisible(dev.off())
```

```{r}
)
```

```{r}
# [1] 72
```

```{r}
otx2_peaks_gl <- ereg_glia_dir %>% 
    filter(TF=="OTX2", sub(".*\\/", "", eRegulon_name) == "+") %>% 
    .$Region %>% 
    unique
# length(otx2_peaks_gl)
# [1] 107
```

Note the TF sets are pretty different:

```{r}
# > all(ereg_glia_dir$TF %in% all_tfs)
# [1] FALSE

# > table(unique(ereg_glia_dir$TF) %in% all_tfs)
# FALSE  TRUE 
#    43    80 
```

Combine neuron+glia targets:

```{r}
otx2_targets_all <- union(otx2_targets, otx2_targets_gl)
# > length(otx2_targets_all)
# [1] 211
```

```{r}
otx2_peaks_all <- union(otx2_peaks, otx2_peaks_gl)
# > length(otx2_peaks_all)
# [1] 388
```

### Scatterplot expression

```{r}
list(
    neur = otx2_top_neur,
    glia = otx2_top_glia
) %>% 
    lapply(function(x) rna_group_mean_cpm[otx2_targets_all, x]) %>% 
    lapply(apply, 1, mean) %>% 
    do.call(cbind, .) %>% 
    as.data.frame %>% 
    rownames_to_column("gene") %>% 
    ggplot(
        aes(log10(neur), log10(glia), label=gene)
    ) + 
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linewidth = 0.25, linetype = "dashed") + 
    geom_point(shape=16, size=1, alpha=0.7) +
    geom_text_repel(size=2, family="ArialMT") +
    labs(
        title="OTX2 Target Genes", 
        x = "OTX2+ neurons (log10 cpm)",
        y = "OTX2+ glia (log10 cpm)"
    ) +
    theme_md_classic()
```


```{r}
ggsave(

)
```

Some very distinct outliers.
Let's grab those with biggest differences

```{r}

    neur = otx2_top_neur,

    mutate(diff = neur - glia) %>%  # high pos neur-specific; low neg glia-specific
```

### (!) Add in peaks differences

```{r}
otx2_neur_v_glia_peaks <- list(
    neur = otx2_top_neur,
    glia = otx2_top_glia
) %>% 
    lapply(function(x) atac_group_mean_cpm_z[otx2_peaks_all, x]) %>% 
    lapply(apply, 1, mean) %>% 
    do.call(cbind, .) %>% 
    as.data.frame %>% 
    mutate(diff = neur - glia) %>%  # high pos neur-specific; low neg glia-specific
    arrange(diff) 
```

```{r}
# top_otx2_targets <- c(top_otx2_neur_targets, top_otx2_glia_targets)
```

Start by plotting all genes/peaks against each other (can be multiple peaks
per gene).

```{r}
otx2_neur_v_glia_genes_peaks <- bind_rows(ereg_neur_dir, ereg_glia_dir) %>% 
    filter(TF == "OTX2") %>% 
    select(Gene, Region, importance_TF2G, importance_R2G) %>% 
    left_join(
        rename(
            rownames_to_column(otx2_neur_v_glia_genes, "Gene"),
            neur_gene = neur,
            glia_gene = glia,
            diff_gene = diff
        ),
        by = "Gene"
    ) %>% 
    left_join(
        rename(
            rownames_to_column(otx2_neur_v_glia_peaks, "Region"),
```

```{r}
otx2_neur_v_glia_genes_peaks_lfc %>%
```


Do they overlap the target gene?


```{r}
pks_gr <- otx2_neur_v_glia_genes_peaks_lfc %>% 
    (function(x) {
        gr <- GRanges(x$Region)
        mcols(gr) <- x[, colnames(x) != "Region"]
        gr
    }) 

# total peaks:
# > length(pks_gr)
# 436

# overlap any gene
findOverlaps(pks_gr, gtf) %>% 
    queryHits %>% 
    unique %>% 
    length
# 329

# contain any TSS
findOverlaps(pks_gr, tsses) %>% 
    queryHits %>% 
    unique %>% 
    length
# 74

# within 500bp of any TSS
findOverlaps(pks_gr, tsses, maxgap=500) %>% 
    queryHits %>% 
    unique %>% 
    length
# 121

# === targets only ===

# overlap target gene
findOverlaps(pks_gr, gtf) %>% 
    as.data.frame %>% 
    mutate(
        query_gn   = pks_gr$Gene[queryHits],
        subject_gn = gtf$gene_id[subjectHits],
        match = query_gn == subject_gn
    ) %>% 
    # only if target gene
    subset(match) %>% 
    # count only the peaks
    .$queryHits %>% 
    unique %>% 
    length
# 202 

# overlap target TSS
findOverlaps(pks_gr, tsses) %>% # the 126 overlaps
    as.data.frame %>%
    mutate(
        query_gn   = pks_gr$Gene[queryHits],
        subject_gn = tsses$gene[subjectHits],
        match = query_gn == subject_gn
    ) %>%
    # only if target gene TSS
    subset(match) %>% 
    # count only the peaks
    .$queryHits %>% 
    unique %>% 
    length
# 57 match

# within 500bp of target TSS
findOverlaps(pks_gr, tsses, maxgap=500) %>% 
    as.data.frame %>%
    mutate(
        query_gn   = pks_gr$Gene[queryHits],
        subject_gn = tsses$gene[subjectHits],
        match = query_gn == subject_gn
    ) %>% 
    # only if target gene TSS
    subset(match) %>% 
    # count only the peaks
    .$queryHits %>% 
    unique %>% 
    length
# 90
```

#### Fisher's exact

Overlaps in peaks or what

```{r}
thr_gene <- 0.75     # log2FC gene
thr_peak <- 0.75     # log2FC peak

otx2_loci <- otx2_neur_v_glia_genes_peaks_lfc %>%
    mutate(concordant = sign(lfc_gene) == sign(lfc_peak),
           bias = case_when(
               concordant & lfc_gene > thr_gene & lfc_peak > thr_peak ~ "neur",
               concordant & lfc_gene < -thr_gene & lfc_peak < -thr_peak ~ "glia",
               TRUE ~ "other"
           )) %>%
    filter(bias != "other")
```

```{r}
ereg_both <- bind_rows(ereg_neur_dir, ereg_glia_dir)

# co-TFs (non-OTX2) that appear in the same peak AND regulate the same target gene
cotf_by_region <- ereg_both %>%
    filter(
        Region %in% otx2_loci$Region,
        Gene   %in% otx2_loci$Gene,
        stringr::str_ends(eRegulon_name, "\\+/\\+")
    ) %>%
    group_by(Gene, Region) %>%
    summarise(cotfs = list(setdiff(unique(TF), "OTX2")), .groups = "drop")

loci_with_cotf <- otx2_loci %>%
    inner_join(cotf_by_region, by = c("Gene","Region")) %>%
    filter(lengths(cotfs) > 0)
```

Single TF enrichment:

```{r}
# explode to one row per TF
tf_long <- loci_with_cotf %>%
    select(Gene, Region, bias, lfc_gene, lfc_peak, importance_TF2G, cotfs) %>%
    unnest_longer(cotfs, values_to = "TF")

# build 2x2 per TF and run Fisher
enrich_tf <- tf_long %>%
    count(TF, bias) %>%
    tidyr::complete(TF, bias = c("neur","glia"), fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    group_by(TF) %>%
    summarise(
        neur = n[bias=="neur"],
        glia = n[bias=="glia"],
        odds_ratio = (neur + 0.5) / (glia + 0.5),   # add 0.5 to stabilise
        p = fisher.test(matrix(c(neur, glia,
                                 sum(tf_long$bias=="neur")-neur,
                                 sum(tf_long$bias=="glia")-glia), nrow=2))$p.value,
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, "BH"),
           side  = ifelse(odds_ratio > 1, "neur_enriched", "glia_enriched")) %>%
    arrange(p_adj)

# > head(enrich_tf, 20) %>% print.data.frame
#        TF neur glia odds_ratio            p      p_adj          side
```

#### TF-pair co-enrichment

TF pairs that co-enrich?

```{r}
library(purrr)
```


```{r}
# limit pair explosion by capping max TFs per locus (optional but sensible)
loci_pairs <- loci_with_cotf %>%
    mutate(
        cotfs = map(cotfs, ~head(.x, 8)),  # optional cap to 8 TFs per locus
        pairs = map(
            cotfs,
            ~ if (length(.x) >= 2)
                combn(sort(unique(.x)), 2, FUN = paste, collapse = "::")
            else
                character(0)
        )
    ) %>%
    unnest_longer(pairs, keep_empty = FALSE)

pair_long <- loci_pairs %>%
    select(Gene, Region, bias, pairs)

enrich_pairs <- pair_long %>%
    count(pairs, bias) %>%
    complete(pairs, bias = c("neur","glia"), fill = list(n=0)) %>%
    group_by(pairs) %>%
    summarise(
        neur = n[bias=="neur"],
        glia = n[bias=="glia"],
        odds_ratio = (neur + 0.5) / (glia + 0.5),
        p = fisher.test(matrix(c(neur, glia,
                                 sum(pair_long$bias=="neur")-neur,
                                 sum(pair_long$bias=="glia")-glia), nrow=2))$p.value,
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, "BH"),
           side = ifelse(odds_ratio > 1, "neur_enriched", "glia_enriched")) %>%
    arrange(p_adj)
```

### New network: diff peaks/genes, same-peak TFs [!] (AND GLIA EREGS)

Taking the top neur_v_glia genes/peaks, filtering for concordant (DAR) peaks,
and then also including TFs that also bind within those same peaks.

```{r}
edges <- otx2_top_neur_v_glia_genes_peaks %>% 
    filter(sign(diff_gene) == sign(diff_peak)) %>% 
    filter(abs(diff_gene) > 0.25, abs(diff_peak) > 0.25) %>% # did nothing
    left_join(
        filter(ereg_neur_dir, Gene %in% .$Gene, Region %in% .$Region) %>% select(Gene, Region, TF, regulation), 
        .,
        by = c("Gene", "Region")
    ) %>% 
    mutate(from=TF, to=Gene, dir=ifelse(regulation==1, "+", "-")) %>% 
    distinct()
```



```{r}
edges <- bind_rows(ereg_neur_dir) %>% 
    filter(
        Gene %in% top_otx2_targets,
        importance_TF2G > 1.5 
    ) %>% 
    mutate(dir = sub(".*_(.*)/.*", "\\1", eRegulon_name))  %>%  # "+" or "-"
    transmute(from = TF, to = Gene, dir, TF2G = importance_TF2G) %>% 
    distinct()

nodes <- tibble(name = unique(c(edges[[1]], edges[[2]]))) 
```

For nodes, get expression of genes in those two groupings.

```{r}
nodes <- list(
    neur_exp = otx2_top_neur,
    glia_exp = otx2_top_glia
) %>% 
    lapply(function(x) rna_group_mean_cpm[nodes$name, x]) %>% 
    lapply(apply, 1, mean) %>% 
    do.call(cbind, .) %>% 
    as.data.frame %>% 
    rownames_to_column("name") %>% 
    left_join(nodes, ., by = "name")

nodes$is_tf <- nodes$name %in% all_tfs
```


```{r}
# --- graph object + centrality for node sizing
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = nodes)

# betweenness on the directed graph; use normalized for scale-friendliness
#
# from documentation:
# "The vertex and edge betweenness are (roughly) defined by the number of 
# geodesics (shortest paths) going through a vertex or an edge."
# V(g)$betweenness <- betweenness(g, directed = TRUE, normalized = TRUE)
# V(g)$score      <- nodes$score

V(g)$neur_exp        <- nodes$neur_exp
V(g)$glia_exp        <- nodes$glia_exp
V(g)$lfc_neur_v_glia <- log2(nodes$neur_exp / nodes$glia_exp)
V(g)$is_tf           <- nodes$is_tf

E(g)$dir  <- edges$dir
E(g)$TF2G <- edges$TF2G

```

Same plot but clip positive z @ 4 (lazy way to make the -4 color darker)

```{r}
geneAUC_neur_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z[intersect(tel_glut_regulons, lge_main_regulons), c(tel_glut_rgnt, lge_main_group)] %>% 
    (function(x) {
        rownames(x) <- gsub("_", " ", rownames(x))

        name = "regulon (z)",
        col = col_fun,
        row_names_gp    = gpar(fontsize = 6, fontfamily = "ArialMT"),
        column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6, fontfamily = "ArialMT"),

            title_gp  = gpar(fontsize = 6, fontface="bold", fontfamily = "ArialMT"),
            labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6, fontfamily = "ArialMT")

    ) -> hm
```

```{r}
list(

    lapply(function(x) rowMeans(geneAUC_neur_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z[, x])) %>%

    apply(1, function(x) x[2] - x[1]) %>%
    .[sub(".*\\/", "", names(.)) == "+"] %>% # require positive peak-to-gene relationship
    split(., sub("_.*", "", names(.))) %>%  # split by TF
    lapply(function(x) x[which.max(abs(x))]) %>% # max difference
```

### Scatterplot absolutes

The one downside here is a lack of background normalization, in the sense that
some of these regulons might be basically consitutive across neurons, and so
not very informative.

### (!) Scatterplot regulon, enrichment vs. background

Instead of comparing TEL Glut vs. LGE, I will compare each vs. everything else
in that matrix.

```{r}
list(
    tel_glut = tel_glut_rgnt,
    lge = lge_main_group,
    background = setdiff(
        colnames(geneAUC_neur_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z),
        c(tel_glut_rgnt, lge_main_group)
    )
) %>% 
    lapply(function(x) rowMeans(geneAUC_neur_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z[, x])) %>% 
    do.call(cbind, .) %>% 
    .[grep("direct", rownames(.)), ] %>% 
    (function(x) x[, 1:2] - x[, 3]) %>% 
    .[sub(".*\\/", "", rownames(.)) == "+", ] %>% # require positive peak-to-gene relationship
    as.data.frame %>% 
    rownames_to_column("regulon") %>% 
    mutate(
        regulon = sub("_direct", " ", regulon),
        regulon = sub("_(.\\/.)$", " (\\1)", regulon)
    ) -> tel_glut_lge_df_coenr_reg

tel_glut_lge_df_coenr_reg %>% 
    ggplot(
        aes(tel_glut, lge, label = regulon)
    ) + 
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth=0.25) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth=0.25) +
    geom_point(size = 1, shape = 16, alpha = 0.7) + 
    geom_text_repel(
        size=2, family="ArialMT",
        min.segment.length = 0
    ) + # make extra small just to have something... | saved w/ 0.5
    # geom_text_repel(size=1.5, family="ArialMT") + 
    ggpubr::stat_cor() +
    labs(
        title = "Diff. Regulon z-score\nvs. background",
        x = "TEL Glut",
        y = "LGE"
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip="off") +
    theme_md_classic()
```

```{r}
            ifelse(

                "LGE",
                "Other"
            )

        color_group = factor(color_group, levels = c("TEL Glut", "LGE", "Other")),
        Grouping = as.character(Grouping),
        Grouping = ifelse(
            grepl("(LGE|MGE|CGE)", Grouping),
            sub("_", "-", Grouping),
            Grouping
        ),
        Grouping = sub("_", " ", Grouping)

    split(., .$TF) %>%

                title = nm
            ) + 
            theme_md_classic()
```

```{r}
    reshape2::melt(

        varnames = c("TF", "Grouping"), 
        value.name = "gene_AUC"
    ) %>% mutate(TF = sub("_.*", "", TF)),
    by = c("TF", "Grouping")
) %>% 
    mutate(
        color_group = ifelse(
            Grouping %in% tel_glut_rgnt,
            "TEL Glut",
            ifelse(
                Grouping %in% lge_main_group,
                "LGE",
                "Other"
            )
        ),
        color_group = factor(color_group, levels = c("TEL Glut", "LGE", "Other")),
        Grouping = as.character(Grouping),
        Grouping = ifelse(
            grepl("(LGE|MGE|CGE)", Grouping),
            sub("_", "-", Grouping),
            Grouping
        ),
        Grouping = sub("_", " ", Grouping)
    ) %>% 
    split(., .$TF) %>% 
    Map(function(x, nm) {
        ggplot(x, aes(log10(Exp), gene_AUC, color = color_group, label = Grouping)) +
            geom_point() + 
            geom_text_repel(min.segment.length=0, family="ArialMT", size=2) +
            scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "blue", "black")) +
            labs(
                x = "TF Expression (log10 CPM)",
                y = "+/+ eRegulon (gene AUC)",
                title = nm
            ) + 
            theme_md_classic()
    }, ., names(.)) %>% 
    unname %>% 
    c(nrow = 3, guides = "collect") %>% 
    do.call(wrap_plots, .)
```

### Get Functional gene sets from co-enriched

based on the stringdb enrichments, have defined some of these functional 
gene modules, and i want to see how they look through the taxonomy.

```{r}

# Strict gene sets: restricted to genes actually present in the TEL Glut–LGE shared list
lge_tel_glut_genesets_full <- list(

    # Canonical MAGUK / SAPAP / PSD scaffold axis.
    # Best "core PSD" readout for the shared TEL Glut–LGE module.
    psd_core_scaffold = c(
        "DLG1",
        "DLG2",
        "DLG4",
        "DLGAP2",
        "DLGAP3",
        "DLGAP4",
        "LRRC7",
        "SYNGAP1",
        "CNKSR2"
    ),

    # Genes more tied to spine structure / spine-associated postsynaptic compartment,
    # rather than just the core scaffold itself.
    spine_remodeling = c(
        "IQSEC2",
        "PTK2B",
        "ACTN1",
        "SYNPO",
        "SIPA1L1",
        "RIN1",
        "RAP2A",
        "RAPGEF5",
        "RASAL1"
    ),

    # Ca2+-responsive postsynaptic signaling / plasticity module.
    # Useful for testing whether a taxon carries the activity-dependent part
    # of the shared program, not just scaffold genes.
    calcium_plasticity = c(
        "CAMK2A",
        "CAMK1D",
        "CAMKK1",
        "CAMKK2",
        "PPP3CA",
        "PPP3R1",
        "ITPR1",
        "RYR2",
        "SLC8A2",
        "CACNA1C",
        "CACNA1E",
        "CACNA1F",
        "KCNIP3",
        "KCNIP4",
        "HPCAL4",
        "NECAB1",
        "PTK2B",
        "KCNJ4",
        "KCNH1"
    ),

    # Small-GTPase / Ras-Rap signaling adjacent to the PSD.
    # Good for asking whether the shared program includes the
    # signaling/remodeling layer and not only structural PSD genes.
    ras_rap_psd_signaling = c(
        "SYNGAP1",
        "IQSEC2",
        "RAP2A",
        "RAPGEF5",
        "RASAL1",
        "RIN1",
        "SIPA1L1",
        "ARAP1",
        "RASGEF1A",
        "PTPN11",
        "SPRED1"
    ),

    # AMPAR-proximal / receptor-organization module.
    # Kept strict to genes actually in the shared list; do not force in
    # GRIA1 or GRIN2B here if absent from this dataset.
    ampar_receptor_proximal = c(
        "GRIA2",
        "GSG1L",
        "DLG1",
        "DLG2",
        "DLG4",
        "DLGAP2",
        "DLGAP3",
        "DLGAP4",
        "SYNGAP1",
        "CAMK2A",
        "PTK2B",
        "PTPN11"
    ),

    # Broader circuit-assembly / input-maturation genes.
    # This is less "PSD core" and more "wiring / synapse maturation".
    wiring_synapse_maturation = c(
        "TYRO3",
        "NTRK3",
        "CELSR2",
        "SLIT3",
        "ADGRB2",
        "PTPN11",
        "SPRED1"
    ),

    # Secondary/supporting signal: neuronal RNA-processing / maturation.
    # Not as specific as the PSD story, but useful to ask whether the shared
    # program extends into post-transcriptional maturation.
    neuronal_splicing_maturation = c(
        "RBFOX1",
        "RBFOX3",
        "CELF1",
        "CELF2",
        "CELF5",
        "MBNL2",
        "HNRNPLL"
    ),

    # High-risk supplementary signal.
    # Split structural cilia genes from ciliary GPCR/signaling genes so you can
    # distinguish "generic cilia load" from a more neuron-like ciliary signal.
    cilia_structural = c(
        "CFAP57",
        "CFAP73",
        "CFAP74",
        "CYS1",
        "DZIP1L",
        "SSX2IP",
        "DNAAF10",
        "DNHD1",
        "RSPH10B",
        "NEK10"
    ),

    cilia_signaling = c(
        "HTR6",
        "NPY5R"
    ),
    
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Exploratory comparator sets: NOT restricted to the current TEL Glut–LGE list
    # These are for follow-up taxonomy comparisons, not for claiming they were
    # part of the original shared-gene result.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    # Candidate interneuron / CIN excitatory-input module.
    # This is meant as a comparison set for MGE/CIN-like lineages, where one
    # might expect more ERBB4 / GRIA4-type flavor than the TEL Glut–LGE core.
    mge_cin_excitatory_input = c(
        "ERBB4",
        "GRIA4",
        "GRIA2",
        "DLG1",
        "DLG4",
        "PTK2B",
        "CAMK2A"
    ),

    # Very small discriminator set for a more "principal/spiny-recipient-like"
    # postsynaptic program.
    principal_spiny_like_psd = c(
        "DLGAP2",
        "DLGAP3",
        "DLGAP4",
        "LRRC7",
        "SYNGAP1",
        "CAMK2A",
        "PTK2B",
        "ACTN1",
        "SYNPO",
        "GRIA2"
    )
)

# "Spiny glutamatergic recipient" hypothesis:
# useful for the question "is this more spine-based / principal-or-MSN-like?"
lge_tel_glut_genesets_full$spiny_glut_recipient <- unique(c(
    lge_tel_glut_genesets_full$psd_core_scaffold,
    c("ACTN1", "SYNPO", "PTK2B", "CAMK2A", "GRIA2")
))

# # Convenient broader unions for plotting / scoring
# lge_tel_glut_genesets$psd_broad <- unique(c(
#     lge_tel_glut_genesets$psd_core_scaffold,
#     lge_tel_glut_genesets$spine_remodeling,
#     lge_tel_glut_genesets$ampar_receptor_proximal,
#     lge_tel_glut_genesets$calcium_plasticity
# ))

lge_tel_glut_genesets_inenr <- lapply(
    lge_tel_glut_genesets_full,
    function(x) x[x %in% tel_glut_lge_coenr_genes_and_regs$Gene]
)

# mapply(setdiff, lge_tel_glut_genesets_full, lge_tel_glut_genesets_inenr) %>% 
#     .[lengths(.)>0]

# $mge_cin_excitatory_input
# [1] "ERBB4" "GRIA4"
```

### Heatmap across taxonomy (by GE_RegionNT_Comp)

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inputs assumed to already exist:
#   rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z   # matrix: rows = genes, cols = taxonomy groups
#   lge_tel_glut_genesets_inenr # named list of gene vectors
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---- font settings ----
gp6 <- gpar(
    fontsize   = 6,
    fontfamily = "ArialMT",
    fontface   = "plain"
)

# # ---- keep only genes that are actually present in the matrix ----
# genesets_plot <- lapply(
#     lge_tel_glut_genesets_full,
#     function(x) unique(x[x %in% rownames(rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z)])
# )
# genesets_plot <- genesets_plot[lengths(genesets_plot) > 0]

# ---- stack all gene sets into one row mapping table ----
# genes are allowed to recur across sets
row_map <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(lge_tel_glut_genesets_full), function(gs) {
        data.frame(
            geneset = gs,
            gene    = lge_tel_glut_genesets_full[[gs]],
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
    })
)

# unique internal row IDs so duplicate genes can appear multiple times
row_map$row_id <- make.unique(paste(row_map$geneset, row_map$gene, sep = "__"))

# ---- assemble plotting matrix ----
mat_plot <- rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z[row_map$gene, , drop = FALSE]
rownames(mat_plot) <- row_map$row_id

# row labels shown on plot = original gene symbols
row_labels <- row_map$gene

# preserve the gene-set order from the list
row_split <- factor(row_map$geneset, levels = names(lge_tel_glut_genesets_full))

# ---- optional: preserve current column order exactly ----
# col_ord <- colnames(mat_plot)
# mat_plot <- mat_plot[, col_ord, drop = FALSE]

# ---- color scale for z-scores ----
# cap at 4 so a few extreme values do not wash everything out
zlim <- max(abs(mat_plot), na.rm = TRUE)
zlim <- min(4, ceiling(zlim * 10) / 10)

colnames(mat_plot) <- gsub("_", " ", colnames(mat_plot))

# ---- heatmap ----
ht <- Heatmap(
    mat_plot,
    name = "RNA z",
    col  = col_fun,
    na_col = "grey90",

    # keep order as supplied
    cluster_rows = FALSE,
    cluster_columns = TRUE,
    cluster_row_slices = FALSE,
    cluster_column_slices = FALSE,

    # split rows by gene set, with visible gaps between sections
    row_split = row_split,
    row_gap   = unit(2, "mm"),

    # names
    show_row_names    = TRUE,
    show_column_names = TRUE,
    row_labels        = row_labels,

    row_names_side = "left",
    row_names_gp   = gp6,
    column_names_gp = gp6,
    column_names_rot = 45,
    row_names_max_width = max_text_width(row_labels, gp = gp6) + unit(2, "mm"),

    # slice titles = gene set names
    row_title_gp  = gp6,
    row_title_rot = 0,

    # legend text
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
        title_gp  = gp6,
        labels_gp = gp6
    ),

    # borders / dendrograms
    border = FALSE,
    show_row_dend = FALSE,
    show_column_dend = FALSE
)

draw(
    ht,
    heatmap_legend_side = "right"
)
```


```{r}
    fontface   = "plain"
)

# # ---- keep only genes that are actually present in the matrix ----
# genesets_plot <- lapply(
#     lge_tel_glut_genesets_full,
#     function(x) unique(x[x %in% rownames(rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z)])
# )
# genesets_plot <- genesets_plot[lengths(genesets_plot) > 0]

# ---- stack all gene sets into one row mapping table ----
# genes are allowed to recur across sets
row_map <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(lge_tel_glut_genesets_full), function(gs) {
        data.frame(
            geneset = gs,
            gene    = lge_tel_glut_genesets_full[[gs]],
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
    })
)

# unique internal row IDs so duplicate genes can appear multiple times
row_map$row_id <- make.unique(paste(row_map$geneset, row_map$gene, sep = "__"))

# ---- assemble plotting matrix ----
mat_plot <- rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z[row_map$gene, , drop = FALSE]
rownames(mat_plot) <- row_map$row_id

# row labels shown on plot = original gene symbols
row_labels <- row_map$gene

# preserve the gene-set order from the list
row_split <- factor(row_map$geneset, levels = names(lge_tel_glut_genesets_full))

# ---- optional: preserve current column order exactly ----
# col_ord <- colnames(mat_plot)
# mat_plot <- mat_plot[, col_ord, drop = FALSE]

# ---- color scale for z-scores ----
# cap at 4 so a few extreme values do not wash everything out
zlim <- max(abs(mat_plot), na.rm = TRUE)
zlim <- min(4, ceiling(zlim * 10) / 10)


### SUBSET MATRIX
cols_keep <- c(
    lge_main_group, tel_glut_rgnt, 
    grep("MGE", colnames(mat_plot), value=TRUE)
)
mat_plot <- mat_plot[, cols_keep]

colnames(mat_plot) <- gsub("_", " ", colnames(mat_plot))

# ---- heatmap ----
ht <- Heatmap(
    mat_plot,
    name = "RNA z",
    col  = col_fun,
    na_col = "grey90",

    # keep order as supplied
    cluster_rows = FALSE,
    cluster_columns = TRUE,
    cluster_row_slices = FALSE,
    cluster_column_slices = FALSE,

    # split rows by gene set, with visible gaps between sections
    row_split = row_split,
    row_gap   = unit(2, "mm"),

    # names
    show_row_names    = TRUE,
    show_column_names = TRUE,
    row_labels        = row_labels,

    row_names_side = "left",
    row_names_gp   = gp6,
    column_names_gp = gp6,
    column_names_rot = 45,
    row_names_max_width = max_text_width(row_labels, gp = gp6) + unit(2, "mm"),

    # slice titles = gene set names
    row_title_gp  = gp6,
    row_title_rot = 0,

    # legend text
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
        title_gp  = gp6,
        labels_gp = gp6
    ),

    # borders / dendrograms
    border = FALSE,
    show_row_dend = FALSE,
    show_column_dend = FALSE
)

draw(
    ht,
    heatmap_legend_side = "right"
)
```

```{r}
    width=5, height=9
)
draw(ht, heatmap_legend_side = "right")
invisible(dev.off())
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Curated representative terms for the first UpSet plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------
terms_keep <- tribble(
    ~category,       ~term_description,                                                 ~term_label,
    "GO Component",  "Postsynaptic density",                                            "GO CC: Postsynaptic density",
    "GO Component",  "Dendritic spine",                                                 "GO CC: Dendritic spine",
    "GO Component",  "Glutamatergic synapse",                                           "GO CC: Glutamatergic synapse",
    "GO Component",  "Somatodendritic compartment",                                     "GO CC: Somatodendritic compartment",
    "GO Component",  "Neuron projection",                                               "GO CC: Neuron projection",
    "Reactome",      "Unblocking of NMDA receptors, glutamate binding and activation",  "Reactome: NMDA unblocking",
    "Reactome",      "Trafficking of AMPA receptors",                                   "Reactome: AMPA trafficking",
    "Reactome",      "Ras activation upon Ca2+ influx through NMDA receptor",           "Reactome: Ras after NMDA/Ca2+",
    "Reactome",      "Neurotransmitter receptors and postsynaptic signal transmission", "Reactome: Postsynaptic signaling",
    "Reactome",      "Neurexins and neuroligins",                                       "Reactome: Neurexin/neuroligin",
    "GO Function",   "Calmodulin-dependent protein kinase activity",                    "GO MF: CaM kinase activity",
    "GO Process",    "Calcium ion import across plasma membrane",                       "GO BP: Calcium import",
    "STRING clusters",        "Postsynaptic cell membrane, and Protein-protein interactions at synapses", "STRING: Postsynapse & PPI"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Build named list: one character vector of genes per term
# ------------------------------------------------------------
term_sets <- lge_tel_glut_stringenr %>%
    semi_join(
        terms_keep,
        by = c("category", "term_description")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
        terms_keep,
        by = c("category", "term_description")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        gene_vec = str_split(matching_protein, ",\\s*"),
        gene_vec = lapply(gene_vec, function(x) unique(x[nzchar(x)]))
    ) %>%
    arrange(match(term_label, terms_keep$term_label)) %>%
    transmute(term_label, gene_vec) %>%
    { setNames(.$gene_vec, .$term_label) }

# optional sanity check
# str(term_sets)
```

#### Heatmap PC1 for terms  (by GE_RegionNT_Comp)

```{r}
rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_select_terms_pc1 <- term_sets %>%
    lapply(function(genes) {
        mat <- rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z[
            intersect(genes, rownames(rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z)),
            ,
            drop = FALSE
        ]
        mat <- mat[apply(mat, 1, function(x) all(is.finite(x))), , drop = FALSE]
        
        if (nrow(mat) == 0) {
            out <- rep(NA_real_, ncol(rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z))
            names(out) <- colnames(rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z)
            return(out)
        }
        
        if (nrow(mat) == 1) {
            out <- as.numeric(mat[1, ])
            names(out) <- colnames(mat)
            return(out)
        }
        
        pc1 <- prcomp(t(mat), center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)$x[, 1]
        mod_mean <- colMeans(mat)
        if (is.finite(cor(pc1, mod_mean)) && cor(pc1, mod_mean) < 0) {
            pc1 <- -pc1
        }
        pc1
    }) %>%
    do.call(rbind, .)
```

##### Heatmap genes for new terms (by GE_RegionNT_Comp)

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inputs assumed to already exist:
#   rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z   # matrix: rows = genes, cols = taxonomy groups
#   lge_tel_glut_genesets_inenr # named list of gene vectors
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---- font settings ----
gp6 <- gpar(
    fontsize   = 6,
    fontfamily = "ArialMT",
    fontface   = "plain"
)

# # ---- keep only genes that are actually present in the matrix ----
# genesets_plot <- lapply(
#     lge_tel_glut_genesets_full,
#     function(x) unique(x[x %in% rownames(rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z)])
# )
# genesets_plot <- genesets_plot[lengths(genesets_plot) > 0]

# ---- stack all gene sets into one row mapping table ----
# genes are allowed to recur across sets
row_map <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(names(string_modules), function(gs) {
        data.frame(
            geneset = gs,
            gene    = string_modules[[gs]],
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
    })
)

# unique internal row IDs so duplicate genes can appear multiple times
row_map$row_id <- make.unique(paste(row_map$geneset, row_map$gene, sep = "__"))

# ---- assemble plotting matrix ----
mat_plot <- rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z[row_map$gene, , drop = FALSE]
rownames(mat_plot) <- row_map$row_id

# row labels shown on plot = original gene symbols
row_labels <- row_map$gene

# preserve the gene-set order from the list
row_split <- factor(row_map$geneset, levels = names(string_modules))

# ---- optional: preserve current column order exactly ----
# col_ord <- colnames(mat_plot)
# mat_plot <- mat_plot[, col_ord, drop = FALSE]

# ---- color scale for z-scores ----
# cap at 4 so a few extreme values do not wash everything out
zlim <- max(abs(mat_plot), na.rm = TRUE)
zlim <- min(4, ceiling(zlim * 10) / 10)

colnames(mat_plot) <- gsub("_", " ", colnames(mat_plot))

# ---- heatmap ----
ht <- Heatmap(
    mat_plot,
    name = "RNA z",
    col  = col_fun,
    na_col = "grey90",

    # keep order as supplied
    cluster_rows = FALSE,
    cluster_columns = TRUE,
    cluster_row_slices = FALSE,
    cluster_column_slices = FALSE,

    # split rows by gene set, with visible gaps between sections
    row_split = row_split,
    row_gap   = unit(2, "mm"),

    # names
    show_row_names    = TRUE,
    show_column_names = TRUE,
    row_labels        = row_labels,

    row_names_side = "left",
    row_names_gp   = gp6,
    column_names_gp = gp6,
    column_names_rot = 45,
    row_names_max_width = max_text_width(row_labels, gp = gp6) + unit(2, "mm"),

    # slice titles = gene set names
    row_title_gp  = gp6,
    row_title_rot = 0,

    # legend text
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
        title_gp  = gp6,
        labels_gp = gp6
    ),

    # borders / dendrograms
    border = FALSE,
    show_row_dend = FALSE,
    show_column_dend = FALSE
)

draw(
    ht,
    heatmap_legend_side = "right"
)
```

```{r}
pdf(
    file.path(pdir_tel_glut_lge, "heatmap_coenr_string_modules_by_gergntcomp.pdf"),
    width=7, height=9
)
draw(ht, heatmap_legend_side = "right")
invisible(dev.off())
```

##### Heatmap new terms PC1 (by GE_RegionNT_Comp)

```{r}
rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_string_module_pc1 <- string_modules %>%
    lapply(function(genes) {
        mat <- rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z[
            intersect(genes, rownames(rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z)),
            ,
            drop = FALSE
        ]
        mat <- mat[apply(mat, 1, function(x) all(is.finite(x))), , drop = FALSE]
        
        if (nrow(mat) == 0) {
            out <- rep(NA_real_, ncol(rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z))
            names(out) <- colnames(rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z)
            return(out)
        }
        
        if (nrow(mat) == 1) {
            out <- as.numeric(mat[1, ])
            names(out) <- colnames(mat)
            return(out)
        }
        
        pc1 <- prcomp(t(mat), center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)$x[, 1]
        mod_mean <- colMeans(mat)
        if (is.finite(cor(pc1, mod_mean)) && cor(pc1, mod_mean) < 0) {
            pc1 <- -pc1
        }
        pc1
    }) %>%
    do.call(rbind, .)
```

#### Make version with gene set in marginal annotation

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Main expression heatmap matrix
# ------------------------------------------------------------
mat_plot <- rna_by_ge_rgnt_comp_cpm_z

cols_keep <- c(
    lge_main_group, tel_glut_rgnt,
    grep("MGE", colnames(mat_plot), value = TRUE)
)

mat_plot <- mat_plot[c(genes_use, "ERBB4", "GRIA4"), cols_keep, drop = FALSE]
colnames(mat_plot) <- gsub("_", " ", colnames(mat_plot))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Binary membership matrix for row annotation
# ------------------------------------------------------------
annot_sets <- c(
    list(
        selected_60 = genes_use,
        mge_psd = c("ERBB4", "GRIA4")
    ),
    term_sets
)

membership_mat <- sapply(annot_sets, function(gs) {
    as.integer(rownames(mat_plot) %in% gs)
})

membership_mat <- as.matrix(membership_mat)
rownames(membership_mat) <- rownames(mat_plot)

# optional: shorten labels a bit
colnames(membership_mat) <- c(
    "all",
    "MGE PSD",
    names(term_sets)
)
membership_mat <- membership_mat[, -1]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Annotation heatmap on the left
# ------------------------------------------------------------
ha_row <- rowAnnotation(
    membership = membership_mat,
    col = list(membership = c("0" = "white", "1" = "black")),
    border = TRUE,
    # gp = gpar(col = "grey80", lwd = 0.3),
    annotation_name_gp = gp6,
    # annotation_name_rot = 0,
    width = unit(ncol(membership_mat) * 2.2, "mm")
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Main heatmap
# ------------------------------------------------------------
ht <- Heatmap(
    mat_plot,
    name = "RNA (z)",
    left_annotation = ha_row,
    
    row_names_gp = gp6,
    column_names_gp = gp6,
    row_title_gp = gp6,
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
        title = "RNA (z)",
        title_gp = gp6,
        labels_gp = gp6
    )
)

draw(ht)
```

## Another way to ID interesting eregulons?

```{r}
geneAUC_neur_by_group_z[, msn_groups]
```

it's actually basically what i already tried, except here also looking for negative specificity,
and throws in tau index or specificity

```{r}
mat <- geneAUC_neur_by_group_z[, msn_groups, drop = FALSE]
focal <- "STRd D2 StrioMat Hybrid MSN"
others <- setdiff(colnames(mat), focal)

df_spec <- data.frame(
    regulon = rownames(mat),
    focal = mat[, focal],
    max_other = apply(mat[, others, drop = FALSE], 1, max),
    mean_other = rowMeans(mat[, others, drop = FALSE]),
    min_other = apply(mat[, others, drop = FALSE], 1, min)
)

df_spec$delta_max  <- df_spec$focal - df_spec$max_other
df_spec$delta_mean <- df_spec$focal - df_spec$mean_other
df_spec$delta_min  <- df_spec$focal - df_spec$min_other

# optional selectivity metric (simple tau)
tau_fun <- function(x) {
    x <- x - min(x)
    if (max(x) == 0) return(0)
    x <- x / max(x)
    sum(1 - x) / (length(x) - 1)
}
df_spec$tau <- apply(mat, 1, tau_fun)

# focal-positive candidate "code"
top_pos <- df_spec[order(-df_spec$delta_max, -df_spec$delta_mean, -df_spec$tau), ]

# focal-depleted candidate "anti-code"
top_neg <- df_spec[order(df_spec$delta_mean, df_spec$delta_max), ]
```


```{r}
# globally above average (focal > 0.5 in your original z-scaling context),
# specifically highest in the focal group (delta_max > 0.5)
# and preferably selective (tau high).
code_candidates <- subset(
  df_spec,
  focal > 0.5 & delta_max > 0.5
)[order(-subset(df_spec, focal > 0.5 & delta_max > 0.5)$tau), ]

print.data.frame(code_candidates)
```

```{r}
# 1. focal specificity scatter
ggplot(df_spec, aes(delta_mean, focal)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2)

# 2. heatmap of top candidate regulons
top_regs <- head(code_candidates$regulon, 20)
pheatmap::pheatmap(mat[top_regs, ], scale = "none")
Heatmap(mat[top_regs, ], heatmap_legend_param = list(title="eRegulon (z)"))

# 3. focal-vs-nearest-neighbors contrasts
nearby <- c("STRd D2 Matrix MSN", "STRd D2 Striosome MSN", "STR D1D2 Hybrid MSN")
contrast_mat <- sweep(mat[, nearby, drop = FALSE], 1, mat[, focal], FUN = "-")
Heatmap(contrast_mat)
```

```{r, fig.height=6}
# library(circlize)

regs_keep <- c("NCOA3_direct_+/+", "MITF_direct_+/-")

trip <- bind_rows(ereg_neur_dir, ereg_neur_ext) %>%
    filter(eRegulon_name %in% regs_keep)

# > nrow(trip)
# [1] 31
# > length(unique(trip$Gene))
# [1] 28

# choose one ranking metric for target strength
# triplet_rank looks like lower = better, so sort ascending
tg <- trip %>%
    select(eRegulon_name, TF, Gene, triplet_rank, importance_TF2G, importance_R2G,
           importance_x_abs_rho, rho_TF2G, rho_R2G) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    arrange(eRegulon_name, triplet_rank)

# optional: keep only top n genes per regulon
n_top <- 40

tg_top <- tg %>%
    group_by(eRegulon_name) %>%
    slice_head(n = n_top) %>%
    ungroup()

### get rid of genes duplicated within a regulon
tg_top <- tg %>%
    group_by(eRegulon_name, Gene) %>%
    slice_min(order_by = triplet_rank, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    group_by(eRegulon_name) %>%
    slice_head(n = n_top) %>%
    ungroup()

### build expression matrix

# keep duplicated genes across regulons by making unique row IDs
row_df <- tg_top %>%
    mutate(
        row_id = make.unique(paste(eRegulon_name, Gene, sep = " | "))
    ) %>%
    select(row_id, eRegulon_name, Gene, triplet_rank)

mat_expr <- rna_group_mean_cpm_z[row_df$Gene, msn_groups, drop = FALSE]

# restore requested row order and apply unique rownames
mat_expr <- as.matrix(mat_expr)
rownames(mat_expr) <- row_df$row_id


### clean out rows that are all NA or non-informative
keep <- apply(mat_expr, 1, function(x) {
    sum(!is.na(x)) > 1 && sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0
})

mat_expr <- mat_expr[keep, , drop = FALSE]
row_df   <- row_df[keep, , drop = FALSE]

### make a split heatmap with row labels showing just the gene names

ht <- Heatmap(
    t(mat_expr),
    name = "RNA (z)",
    col = colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("blue", "#EEEEEE", "red")),
    na_col = "grey90",
    
    column_split = factor(row_df$eRegulon_name, levels = regs_keep),
    
    column_labels = row_df$Gene,
    # column_names_rot = 90,
    
    row_names_gp   = gp6,
    column_names_gp = gp6,
    row_title_gp  = gp6,
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
        title = "RNA (z)",
        title_gp  = gp6,
        labels_gp = gp6
    )
)

draw(ht)
```

## Plot regulons & enrichment together

```{r}
# --- 1) Heatmap matrix (RegionNT x eRegulon) ---
mat <- t(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_rgnt_z[eregs_cracdl, , drop = FALSE])  # rows = RegionNT, cols = selected regulons

# --- 2) Build the CRACDL log2FC vector per RegionNT (names must match rownames(mat)) ---
df_crac <- bind_rows(Map(
    function(df, nm) data.frame(
        RegionNT   = nm,
        Enrichment = df["CRACDL", "log2FoldChange_shr"]
    ),
    dsres_rna, names(dsres_rna)
))

# keep only RegionNT present in the heatmap, coerce to named numeric vector
v_crac <- df_crac %>%
    filter(RegionNT %in% rownames(mat)) %>%
    arrange(match(RegionNT, rownames(mat))) %>%
    { setNames(.$Enrichment, .$RegionNT) }

# (Optional) symmetric y-limits for nicer visual balance
ylim_max <- max(abs(v_crac), na.rm = TRUE)
ylims <- c(-ylim_max, ylim_max)

# --- 3) Row-side barplot annotation (sticks to heatmap's row order & clustering) ---
ra <- rowAnnotation(
    "CRACDL log2FC" = anno_barplot(
        v_crac[rownames(mat)],            # ensure order matches heatmap rows
        which      = "row",
        border     = FALSE,
        gp         = gpar(fill = "grey65"),
        width      = unit(28, "mm"),
        ylim       = ylims,
        axis_param = list(side = "top")   # axis drawn at the top of the barplot panel
    ),
    annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7)
)

# --- 4) Heatmap (keeps your clustering; annotation on the right) ---
ht <- Heatmap(
    mat,
    name = "regulon (z)",
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_columns = TRUE,
    show_row_names = TRUE,
    show_column_names = TRUE,
    right_annotation = ra
)

pdf(file.path(pdir_crac, "cracdl_regulon_z_with_bar.pdf"), width = 5, height = 7)
draw(ht)
invisible(dev.off())

```

- AMY_MSN lacks CRACDL, but kinda has SMAD3, ZBTB18, and both almost similar
  to STR_MSN
  
So that's kind of an issue. Maybe I'm *missing* some of the negative regulators

```{r}
# --- Top barplot annotation for CRACDL log2FC ---
ta <- HeatmapAnnotation(
    "CRACDL log2FC" = anno_barplot(
        v_crac[ord],
        which      = "column",
        border     = FALSE,
        gp         = gpar(fill = "grey65"),
        height     = unit(18, "mm"),
        ylim       = ylims,
        axis_param = list(side = "right")   # axis on the right side of the bar panel
    ),
    annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7)
)

# --- Heatmap: keep your row clustering, fixed column order, labels rotated 30° and centered ---
ht <- Heatmap(
    mat,
    name               = "regulon (z)",
    cluster_rows       = TRUE,
    cluster_columns    = FALSE,
    column_order       = ord,
    top_annotation     = ta,
    show_row_names     = TRUE,
    show_column_names  = TRUE,
    column_names_side  = "bottom",         # labels under the heatmap
    # column_names_rot   = 30,               # rotate 30°
    # column_names_centered = TRUE,          # center under tiles (available in recent ComplexHeatmap)
    column_names_gp    = gpar(fontsize = 7)
)

pdf(file.path(pdir_crac, "cracdl_regulon_all_z_sideways_topbar.pdf"), width = 7, height = 3)
draw(ht)
invisible(dev.off())

```

```{r}
edges <- cracdl_net$edges
nodes <- cracdl_net$nodes

# re-using this from the TEL Glut vs LGE vignette
# tel_glut_rgnt <- c(
#     "CTX_Glut",
#     "OlfC_Glut",
#     "HiF_Glut",
#     "CLEn_Glut",
#     "AMY_Glut"
# )

# (out-of-order use of expression object)

# TF expression
nodes$TF_exp_tel_glut <- rowMeans(rna_by_rgnt_cpm_z[nodes$TF, tel_glut_rgnt])
nodes$TF_exp_str_msn  <- rna_by_rgnt_cpm_z[nodes$TF, "STR_MSN"]

# max regulon usage (direction adjusted)
# -> negative z for repressive regulons
# geneAUC_neur_by_rgnt_z
nodes$regulon_z_tel_glut <- sapply(nodes$TF, function(tf) {
    if (!tf %in% ereg_neur_dir$TF)
        return(NA)
    # direct only
    ers  <- unique(subset(bind_rows(ereg_neur_dir_pp, ereg_neur_dir_mp), TF == tf)$eRegulon_name)
    erds <- sub(".*_(.)\\/.$", "\\1", ers)
    erm  <- rowMeans(geneAUC_neur_by_rgnt_z[ers, tel_glut_rgnt, drop=FALSE])
    # invert for repressive (so low z-score means high "tf activity")
    scores <- ifelse(erds == "+", erm, -erm)
    # return max
    max(scores)
})

nodes$regulon_z_str_msn <- sapply(nodes$TF, function(tf) {
    if (!tf %in% ereg_neur_dir$TF)
        return(NA)
    # direct only
    ers  <- unique(subset(bind_rows(ereg_neur_dir_pp, ereg_neur_dir_mp), TF == tf)$eRegulon_name)
    erds <- sub(".*_(.)\\/.$", "\\1", ers)
    erm  <- rowMeans(geneAUC_neur_by_rgnt_z[ers, "STR_MSN", drop=FALSE])
    # invert for repressive (so low z-score means high "tf activity")
    scores <- ifelse(erds == "+", erm, -erm)
    # return max
    max(scores)
})
```

```{r}
set.seed(12)
# --- graph object + centrality for node sizing
# g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = cracdl_net$edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = cracdl_net$nodes)

# both of these work... idk
# g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = cracdl_net$edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = tibble(name = unique(c(edges[[1]], edges[[2]]))))
g <- graph_from_data_frame(
    d = transmute(edges, from = TF, to = Gene, dir),
    directed = TRUE,
    vertices = nodes
)

# betweenness on the directed graph; use normalized for scale-friendliness
#
# from documentation:
# "The vertex and edge betweenness are (roughly) defined by the number of 
# geodesics (shortest paths) going through a vertex or an edge."
# V(g)$betweenness <- betweenness(g, directed = TRUE, normalized = TRUE)
# V(g)$score      <- nodes$score

# size for TF_exp, color for regulon
V(g)$TF_exp    <- nodes$TF_exp_tel_glut
V(g)$Regulon_z <- nodes$regulon_z_tel_glut

E(g)$dir <- edges$dir


# --- Draw with ggraph
#
# Plot normal edges and self-loops separately so can control the loops
is_loop <- which(head_of(g, E(g)) == tail_of(g, E(g)))

p1 <- ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
    # non-self edges
    geom_edge_link(
        aes(color = dir),
        end_cap   = circle(1.5, "mm"),
        start_cap = circle(1.5, "mm"),
        # arrow     = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
        arrow     = arrow(length = unit(1, "mm"), type = "closed"),
        # edge_width = 0.6,
        edge_width = 0.25,
        # alpha = 0.8,
        show.legend = TRUE
    ) +
    # self-loops (if any)
    # geom_edge_loop(
    #     aes(color = dir),
    #     # edge_width = 0.6,
    #     end_cap   = circle(0.75, "mm"),
    #     start_cap = circle(0.5, "mm"),
    #     edge_width = 0.25,
    #     # strength = 0.15,
    #     # arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
    #     arrow = arrow(length = unit(1, "mm"), type = "closed"),
    #     show.legend = FALSE
    # ) +
    # nodes
    geom_node_point(
        aes(size = TF_exp, fill = Regulon_z),
        shape = 21, 
        # stroke = 0.4
        stroke = 0.25,
        show.legend = TRUE
    ) +
    geom_node_text(
        aes(label = name),
        repel     = TRUE, 
        size      = 2, 
        vjust     = 0.5,
        family    = "ArialMT"
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(      ######## [!] Note I verified these limits were appropriate for my data
        name = "Max Regulon Activity\n(z-score, negated\nif repressive)",
        low  = "blue", mid = "#EEEEEE", high = "red", # match ComplexHeatmap
        midpoint = 0,
        limits = c(-2, 2),
        oob = scales::squish,
        # limits = c(
        #     min(V(g)$score, na.rm = TRUE),
        #     max(V(g)$score, na.rm = TRUE)
        # )
    ) +
    scale_size_continuous(
        name = "Gene expression\n(z-score)", 
        range = c(0.25, 4),
        limits = c(-2, 3)
    ) +
    scale_edge_color_manual(
        values = c("+" = "black", "-" = "#E60000"),
        name = "Regulation"
    ) +
    # guides(
    #     edge_color = guide_legend(order = 1),
    #     size       = guide_legend(order = 2),
    #     fill       = guide_colorbar(order = 3)
    # ) +
    # theme_graph(base_family = "sans") +
    theme_md_classic() +
    theme(
        legend.position = "right",
        axis.line  = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.text  = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_blank()
    ) + 
    labs(title = "CRACDL Regulon Network\nCTX/OlfC/HiF/CLEn/AMY Glut")
p1
```

# Gangliomic Eminence cells by regions

It's known that cells from the GE migrate to different structures. It won't be
hard to find genes or regulons associated with the MGE or CGE or LGE. 

But do those cells end up becoming more similar in some ways to their 
destination structures? 

Or comparing them, maybe even if not more similar to other cells in destination,
we might still uncover the regulatory programs associated with their migration
route.

```{r}
pdir_ge <- file.path(pdir_plots, "GanglionicEminence")
if (!dir.exists(pdir_ge))
    dir.create(pdir_ge)
```

#### (!) Heatmap correlations by NT 

Basically for GABA. Copy code used for non GE-divided.


```{r}
plt_dir <- file.path(pdir_ge, "heatmap_zscore_cor_ge_rgnt_by_nt")
if (!dir.exists(plt_dir))
    dir.create(plt_dir)

# Build the color function with fixed limits
# col_fun <- colorRamp2(
#     seq(-1, 1, length.out = 100),
#     colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(9, "RdBu")))(100) # default ComplexHeatmap
# )
col_fun <- colorRamp2(c(-1, 0, 1), c("blue", "#EEEEEE", "red"))

for (nt in colnames(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_nt_z)) {
    m <- geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z  
    m <- m[, grep(paste0("_", nt, "$"), colnames(m)), drop=FALSE]
    colnames(m) <- ifelse(
        grepl("(MGE|LGE|CGE)", colnames(m)),
        sub("_", "-", colnames(m)),
        colnames(m)
    )
    colnames(m) <- sub("_", " ", colnames(m))
    
    ht <- Heatmap(
        cor(m), 
        name = paste0("regulon (z)\ncorrelation"), 
        col = col_fun,
        # show_column_names = FALSE,
        column_title = paste(nt, "clusters"),
        # heatmap_legend_param = list(
        #     legend_direction = "horizontal"
        # )
        row_names_gp    = gpar(fontsize = 6, fontfamily = "ArialMT"),
        column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6, fontfamily = "ArialMT"),
        heatmap_legend_param = list(
            title_gp  = gpar(fontsize = 6, fontface="bold", fontfamily = "ArialMT"),
            labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6, fontfamily = "ArialMT")
        )
    ) 
    pdf(file.path(plt_dir, paste0(nt, ".pdf")), width=4, height=3)
    # draw(ht, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom")
    draw(ht)
    invisible(dev.off())
}
```

```{r}
act_by_ge_rgnt <- lapply(colnames(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_z), function(cn) {
    names(which(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_z[,cn] > 1))
})
names(act_by_ge_rgnt) <- colnames(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_z)

# pairwise Jaccard
jaccard <- outer(
    names(act_by_ge_rgnt), names(act_by_ge_rgnt),
    Vectorize(function(a,b){
        A <- act_by_ge_rgnt[[a]]
        B <- act_by_ge_rgnt[[b]]
        length(intersect(A,B)) / length(union(A,B))
    })
)
rownames(jaccard) <- colnames(jaccard) <- names(act_by_ge_rgnt)
```

### Shared regulons: expand to all

Redo the calculation but for the "complete" set (like used for the main big
heatmap)

```{r}
act_by_ge_rgnt_comp <- lapply(colnames(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z), function(cn) {
    names(which(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z[,cn] > 1))
})
names(act_by_ge_rgnt_comp) <- colnames(geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z)

# pairwise Jaccard
jaccard <- outer(
    names(act_by_ge_rgnt_comp), names(act_by_ge_rgnt_comp),
    Vectorize(function(a,b){
        A <- act_by_ge_rgnt_comp[[a]]
        B <- act_by_ge_rgnt_comp[[b]]
        length(intersect(A,B)) / length(union(A,B))
    })
)
rownames(jaccard) <- colnames(jaccard) <- names(act_by_ge_rgnt_comp)
```

## Barplot cor

```{r}
geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z %>% 
    cor %>% 
    .[c("THM_GABA"), ] %>% 
    as.data.frame %>% 
    setNames("cor_regulon_z") %>% 
    rownames_to_column("grouping") %>% 
    filter(grouping!="THM_GABA") %>% 
    arrange(cor_regulon_z) %>% 
    mutate(
        grouping = ifelse(
            grepl("(MGE|LGE|CGE)", grouping),
            sub("_", "-", grouping),
            grouping
        ),
        grouping = sub("_", " ", grouping),
        grouping=factor(grouping, levels=grouping)
    ) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(grouping, cor_regulon_z)) + 
    geom_col(linewidth=0.25, color="black", fill="gray75") + 
    theme_md_classic() + 
    coord_flip(ylim=c(-1,1)) + 
    labs(
        x="cells regrouped by GE origin,\nDominant Region, and Neurotransmitter", 
        y="eRegulon Usage (gene AUC z-score)\ncorrelation with THM GABA"
    ) 
```

#### Avg for all 4 MGE GABA groups

```{r}
mge_gaba_groups <- c("MGE_AMY_GABA","MGE_CTX_GABA","MGE_HiF_GABA","MGE_STR_GABA")

# --- TF -> TF edges
edges <- bind_rows(ereg_neur_dir, ereg_neur_ext) %>% 
    filter(
        Gene %in% sub("_.*", "", eregs_active_mge_gaba),
        TF %in% sub("_.*", "", eregs_active_mge_gaba)
    ) %>% 
    mutate(dir = sub(".*_(.*)/.*", "\\1", eRegulon_name)) %>%  # "+" or "-"
    transmute(from = TF, to = Gene, dir) %>% 
    distinct()

# --- Summarize node activity for fill color
#
# for now, summarize TF activity across the 4 groups for all regulons (but this
# is just a sketch, I don't love this -> later will do these separately for
# each group so the weighting should look distinct when applicable)
tf_activity <- geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z[, mge_gaba_groups] %>% 
    as.data.frame %>% 
    rownames_to_column("ereg") %>% 
    mutate(TF = sub("_.*", "", ereg)) %>% 
    group_by(TF) %>% 
    summarise(across(all_of(mge_gaba_groups), ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>% 
    mutate(mean_z = rowMeans(across(all_of(mge_gaba_groups)), na.rm = TRUE))

nodes <- tibble(name = union(edges$from, edges$to)) %>% 
    left_join(tf_activity %>% select(TF, mean_z), by = c("name" = "TF"))

# --- graph object + centrality for node sizing
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = nodes)

# betweenness on the directed graph; use normalized for scale-friendliness
#
# "The vertex and edge betweenness are (roughly) defined by the number of 
# geodesics (shortest paths) going through a vertex or an edge."
V(g)$betweenness <- betweenness(g, directed = TRUE, normalized = TRUE)
V(g)$mean_z      <- nodes$mean_z

E(g)$dir <- edges$dir

# --- Draw with ggraph
#
# We'll plot normal edges + self-loops separately for good control.
is_loop <- which(head_of(g, E(g)) == tail_of(g, E(g)))

p <- ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
    # non-self edges
    geom_edge_link(
        aes(color = dir),
        end_cap   = circle(3, "mm"),
        start_cap = circle(2, "mm"),
        arrow     = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
        edge_width = 0.6,
        alpha = 0.8,
        show.legend = TRUE
    ) +
    # self-loops (if any)
    geom_edge_loop(
        aes(color = dir),
        edge_width = 0.6,
        strength = 0.15,
        arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
        show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    # nodes
    geom_node_point(
        aes(size = betweenness, fill = mean_z),
        shape = 21, stroke = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_node_text(
        aes(label = name),
        repel = TRUE, size = 3.5, vjust = 0.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
        name = "mean regulon z\nin MGE GABA",
        low = muted("blue"), mid = "white", high = muted("red"),
        midpoint = 0, limits = c(min(V(g)$mean_z, na.rm = TRUE),
                                 max(V(g)$mean_z, na.rm = TRUE))
    ) +
    scale_size_continuous(
        name = "Betweenness", range = c(3, 10)
    ) +
    scale_edge_color_manual(
        values = c("+" = "#2C7BB6", "-" = "#D7191C"),
        name = "Regulation"
    ) +
    guides(
        edge_color = guide_legend(order = 1),
        size       = guide_legend(order = 2),
        fill       = guide_colorbar(order = 3)
    ) +
    theme_graph(base_family = "sans") +
    theme(legend.position = "right")

p
```

#### Each MGE GABA group separately

```{r}
for (group_use in mge_gaba_groups) {
    ereg_active <- geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z[, group_use, drop=FALSE] %>% 
        .[apply(., 1, max) > 1, , drop=FALSE] %>% 
        rownames
    
    # --- TF -> TF edges
    edges <- bind_rows(ereg_neur_dir, ereg_neur_ext) %>% 
        filter(
            Gene %in% sub("_.*", "", ereg_active),
            TF %in% sub("_.*", "", ereg_active)
        ) %>% 
        mutate(dir = sub(".*_(.*)/.*", "\\1", eRegulon_name)) %>%  # "+" or "-"
        transmute(from = TF, to = Gene, dir) %>% 
        distinct()
    
    # --- Summarize node activity for fill color
    #
    # for now, summarize TF activity across the 4 groups for all regulons (but this
    # is just a sketch, I don't love this -> later will do these separately for
    # each group so the weighting should look distinct when applicable)
    #
    # but basically, for each TF, take its max regulon score (as a proxy for its
    # activity) [otherwise could use its expression...]
    #
    # then this also averages those maxes across the groups being used...
    tf_activity <- geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z[, group_use, drop=FALSE] %>% 
        as.data.frame %>% 
        rownames_to_column("ereg") %>% 
        mutate(TF = sub("_.*", "", ereg)) %>% 
        group_by(TF) %>% 
        summarise(across(all_of(group_use), ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>% 
        mutate(mean_z = rowMeans(across(all_of(group_use)), na.rm = TRUE))
    
    nodes <- tibble(name = union(edges$from, edges$to)) %>% 
        left_join(tf_activity %>% select(TF, mean_z), by = c("name" = "TF"))
    
    # --- graph object + centrality for node sizing
    g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = nodes)
    
    # betweenness on the directed graph; use normalized for scale-friendliness
    #
    # "The vertex and edge betweenness are (roughly) defined by the number of 
    # geodesics (shortest paths) going through a vertex or an edge."
    V(g)$betweenness <- betweenness(g, directed = TRUE, normalized = TRUE)
    V(g)$mean_z      <- nodes$mean_z
    
    E(g)$dir <- edges$dir
    
    # --- Draw with ggraph
    #
    # We'll plot normal edges + self-loops separately for good control.
    is_loop <- which(head_of(g, E(g)) == tail_of(g, E(g)))
    
    p <- ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
        # non-self edges
        geom_edge_link(
            aes(color = dir),
            end_cap   = circle(0.75, "mm"),
            start_cap = circle(0.5, "mm"),
            # arrow     = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
            arrow     = arrow(length = unit(1, "mm"), type = "closed"),
            # edge_width = 0.6,
            edge_width = 0.25,
            # alpha = 0.8,
            show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        # self-loops (if any)
        geom_edge_loop(
            aes(color = dir),
            # edge_width = 0.6,
            end_cap   = circle(0.75, "mm"),
            start_cap = circle(0.5, "mm"),
            edge_width = 0.25,
            # strength = 0.15,
            # arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(1, "mm"), type = "closed"),
            show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        # nodes
        geom_node_point(
            aes(size = betweenness, fill = mean_z),
            shape = 21, 
            # stroke = 0.4
            stroke = 0.25,
            show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        geom_node_text(
            aes(label = name),
            repel = TRUE, 
            size = 2, 
            vjust = 0.5,
            family = "ArialMT"
        ) +
        scale_fill_gradient2(
            name = "TF activity\n(max regulon z)",
            low = "blue", mid = "#EEEEEE", high = "red", # match ComplexHeatmap
            midpoint = 0, 
            limits = c(-4, 4)
            # limits = c(
            #     min(V(g)$mean_z, na.rm = TRUE),
            #     max(V(g)$mean_z, na.rm = TRUE)
            # )
        ) +
        scale_size_continuous(
            name = "Betweenness", range = c(1, 3)
        ) +
        scale_edge_color_manual(
            values = c("+" = "black", "-" = "#E60000"),
            name = "Regulation"
        ) +
        # guides(
        #     edge_color = guide_legend(order = 1),
        #     size       = guide_legend(order = 2),
        #     fill       = guide_colorbar(order = 3)
        # ) +
        # theme_graph(base_family = "sans") +
        theme_md_classic() +
        theme(
            legend.position = "right",
            axis.line = element_blank(),
            axis.ticks = element_blank(),
            axis.text = element_blank(),
            axis.title = element_blank()
        ) + 
        labs(title = paste(
            sub("_", " ", sub("_", "-", group_use))),
            collapse = ", "
        )
    
    ggsave(
        file.path(pdir_str_ctx, paste0("tf_network_", group_use, ".pdf")),
        p,
        width = 40, height = 40, units = "mm"
    )
}
```

```{r}
    #
    # then this also averages those maxes across the groups being used...
    tf_activity <- geneAUC_neur_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z[, group_use, drop=FALSE] %>% 
        as.data.frame %>% 
        rownames_to_column("ereg") %>% 
        mutate(TF = sub("_.*", "", ereg)) %>% 
        group_by(TF) %>% 
        summarise(across(all_of(group_use), ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>% 
        mutate(mean_z = rowMeans(across(all_of(group_use)), na.rm = TRUE))
    
    nodes <- tibble(name = union(edges$from, edges$to)) %>% 
        left_join(tf_activity %>% select(TF, mean_z), by = c("name" = "TF"))
    
    # --- graph object + centrality for node sizing
    g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = edges, directed = TRUE, vertices = nodes)
    
    # betweenness on the directed graph; use normalized for scale-friendliness
    #
    # "The vertex and edge betweenness are (roughly) defined by the number of 
    # geodesics (shortest paths) going through a vertex or an edge."
    V(g)$betweenness <- betweenness(g, directed = TRUE, normalized = TRUE)
    V(g)$mean_z      <- nodes$mean_z
    
    E(g)$dir <- edges$dir
    
    # --- Draw with ggraph
    #
    # We'll plot normal edges + self-loops separately for good control.
    is_loop <- which(head_of(g, E(g)) == tail_of(g, E(g)))
    
    p <- ggraph(g, layout = "fr") +
        # non-self edges
        geom_edge_link(
            aes(color = dir),
            end_cap   = circle(0.75, "mm"),
            start_cap = circle(0.5, "mm"),
            # arrow     = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
            arrow     = arrow(length = unit(1, "mm"), type = "closed"),
            # edge_width = 0.6,
            edge_width = 0.25,
            # alpha = 0.8,
            show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        # self-loops (if any)
        geom_edge_loop(
            aes(color = dir),
            # edge_width = 0.6,
            end_cap   = circle(0.75, "mm"),
            start_cap = circle(0.5, "mm"),
            edge_width = 0.25,
            # strength = 0.15,
            # arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(1, "mm"), type = "closed"),
            show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        # nodes
        geom_node_point(
            aes(size = betweenness, fill = mean_z),
            shape = 21, 
            # stroke = 0.4
            stroke = 0.25,
            show.legend = FALSE
        ) +
        geom_node_text(
            aes(label = name),
            repel = TRUE, 
            size = 2, 
            vjust = 0.5,
            family = "ArialMT"
        ) +
        scale_fill_gradient2(
            name = "TF activity\n(max regulon z)",
            low = "blue", mid = "#EEEEEE", high = "red", # match ComplexHeatmap
            midpoint = 0, 
            limits = c(-4, 4)
            # limits = c(
            #     min(V(g)$mean_z, na.rm = TRUE),
            #     max(V(g)$mean_z, na.rm = TRUE)
            # )
        ) +
        scale_size_continuous(
            name = "Betweenness", range = c(1, 3)
        ) +
        scale_edge_color_manual(
            values = c("+" = "black", "-" = "#E60000"),
            name = "Regulation"
        ) +
        # guides(
        #     edge_color = guide_legend(order = 1),
        #     size       = guide_legend(order = 2),
        #     fill       = guide_colorbar(order = 3)
        # ) +
        # theme_graph(base_family = "sans") +
        theme_md_classic() +
        theme(
            legend.position = "right",
            axis.line = element_blank(),
            axis.ticks = element_blank(),
            axis.text = element_blank(),
            axis.title = element_blank()
        ) + 
        labs(title = paste(
            sub("_", " ", sub("_", "-", group_use))),
            collapse = ", "
        )
    
    ggsave(
        file.path(pdir_str_ctx, paste0("tf_network_with_ext_", group_use, ".pdf")),
        p,
        width = 40, height = 40, units = "mm"
    )
}
```

Find regulons only active in 1:

```{r}
geneAUC_neur_dir_pp_by_ge_rgnt_comp_z %>% 
    .[, grep("MGE", colnames(.))] %>% 
    .[, grep("GABA", colnames(.))] %>% 
    # .[apply(., 1, function(x) max(x) > 1), ] %>% # only active in MGE GABA
    # apply(1, ">", 1, simplify = FALSE) %>%  
    (function(x) {
        # subset to active somewhere in MGE GABA
        mask <- ifelse(
            sub(".*_(.*)\\/.$", "\\1", rownames(x)) == "+",
            apply(x, 1, function(x) max(x) > 1),
            apply(x, 1, function(x) min(x) < -1)
        )
        x <- x[mask, ]
        # in each group, declare if active (logical)
        setNames(
            ifelse(
                sub(".*_(.*)\\/.$", "\\1", rownames(x)) == "+",
                apply(x, 1, ">",  1, simplify = FALSE),
                apply(x, 1, "<", -1, simplify = FALSE)
            ),
            rownames(x)
        )
    }) %>% 
    .[sapply(., function(x) sum(x)==1)] %>%  # take only if active in 1 group
    sapply(function(x) names(x)[x]) %>%  # get the names
    (function(x) split(names(x), unname(x))) ->  # group by mge gaba group
    unique_eregs_mge_gaba
unique_eregs_mge_gaba
```

```{r}
geneAUC_neur_by_ge_rgnt_z[, c("MGE_STR_GABA", "MGE_CTX_GABA")] %>%
    apply(1, function(x) x[2] - x[1]) %>%

        by = "TF"
```

#### Quick gene summary

ChatGPT making stuff up:

Striatum-bound MGE derivatives (many becoming CINs) keep *Nkx2-1/Isl1/Lhx8* ON,
turn up cholinergic machinery and adhesion/fasciculation components (*AMIGO2*,
*SLITRK6*) and leverage *NGFR/GDNF* signaling—together favoring entry/retention
within the striatal mantle and assembly of local circuits.

Cortex-bound MGE interneurons up-regulate *ECM* editors (*SULF1*, *LTBP1*) that
re-tune responsiveness to long-range cues (*Slit/Netrin/Sema/Eph*) while engaging
vascular programs (*ETS1/FLI1*) that fit the blood-vessel–guided migration model.
Once in the cortical plate, SATB1 switches them from migration to
SST/fast-spiking lineage maturation.

I'm not going for all of it but it's helping to point out some genes that are
interesting to talk about.

(STR) Cholinergic identity/synapse: CHAT, SLC5A7, ACHE, PRIMA1 

(STR) Adhesion/fasciculation: AMIGO2, SLITRK6 
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9796841/
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430182/

(STR) Neurotrophins & receptors: GDNF, NGFR/p75NTR – motility tuning & trophic support



(CTX) ECM/glycan editing: SULF1, LTBP1 – HS/sulfation editing & TGF-b matrix control -> cue availability & substrate. 

(CTX) Vascular/angiogenic TFs: ETS1 (±FLI1) – endothelial program links; migration along vessels. 

(CTX) Migration stop & maturation: SATB1, SST (ETS1 regulon).
